name: elasticsearch_exporter-54487773-blind18
instr:
# elasticsearch_exporter: eighteen undocumented edits, diagnosed without a test suite

A program that reads numbers out of a search-and-analytics server and republishes them for a monitoring system has become unusable. The repository has received 18 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the remote server changed and nothing about the callers changed: the same servers still answer 200 with well-formed JSON, yet the program now publishes almost nothing, and what it does publish is often the opposite of the truth.

Before anything is scraped, an operator writes a YAML file declaring named credential sets, and that file is now judged backwards. An entry naming a certificate but no key is accepted happily, while a complete entry naming an authority, a certificate and a key is refused outright, as is an api-key entry carrying a certificate and key beside it. Entries that should never be accepted at all — one declaring an unsupported kind, or a username with no password — are taken in silence instead, because a failure noticed while reading that file no longer reaches whoever asked for it as an error. Asking for a one-off scrape of an address handed over at request time then fails before any HTTP call is made: a well-formed http address together with the name of a credential set that really does exist comes back complaining that no address was supplied, and it does so whether that set uses a username and password, an api key, AWS credentials or client certificates.
